arcs.name: The Patriarchs
arcs.sub: A man leaves a city he will never see again, on the strength of a promise.

arcs.name: The Exodus
arcs.sub: A nation is carried out of Egypt, and spends forty years learning to trust the One who carried it.

arcs.name: The Judges
arcs.sub: There is no king. Deliverers rise and fall, and every man does what is right in his own eyes.

arcs.name: Kingdom & Exile
arcs.sub: The throne rises, the prophets warn, the walls come down, and the people are carried east.

arcs.name: The Gospel & The Church
arcs.sub: The Word is made flesh, the tomb is emptied, and the message runs to the edge of the empire.

sites.context: Where the journey begins.
sites.description: A paramount Sumerian city near the head of the Persian Gulf, with a moon-god temple complex, courtyard housing and river trade reaching the Indus. Abraham's family departs from here, and never comes back.
sites.name: UR OF THE CHALDEES
sites.place: Sumerian Euphrates basin
sites.quote: And they went forth with them from Ur of the Chaldees, to go into the land of Canaan.

sites.context: The pivot of the migration.
sites.description: A commercial crossroads on the Balikh where Terah settled and died, and where the promise was renewed before Abraham turned southwest toward a land he had never seen.
sites.name: HARAN
sites.place: Upper Euphrates trade hub
sites.quote: So Abram departed, as the LORD had spoken unto him… and Abram was seventy and five years old when he departed out of Haran.

sites.context: The first altar in the land of promise.
sites.description: The first stop inside Canaan, set in the saddle between two mountains that would later stage the blessings and the curses. Joshua renewed the covenant on this ground at the end of his life.
sites.name: SHECHEM
sites.place: The pass between Ebal and Gerizim
sites.quote: And there builded he an altar unto the LORD, who appeared unto him.

sites.context: The family home and the ancestral tomb.
sites.description: The patriarchal home, and the first piece of the promised land actually owned — a burial cave bought at full price, holding Sarah, Abraham, Isaac, Rebekah, Jacob and Leah.
sites.name: HEBRON (MAMRE)
sites.place: The highest city on the Judean ridge
sites.quote: Then Abram removed his tent, and came and dwelt in the plain of Mamre, which is in Hebron, and built there an altar unto the LORD.

sites.context: The southern marker of Israel.
sites.description: The wells at the edge of the Negev, where Abraham and Isaac settled water disputes and swore treaties. "From Dan to Beersheba" became the standard measure of the whole land.
sites.name: BEERSHEBA
sites.place: Wells at the desert threshold
sites.quote: Wherefore he called that place Beersheba; because there they sware both of them.

sites.archaeology: Temple Mount · the threshing floor of Araunah
sites.context: Where the ram was caught in the thicket.
sites.description: The mountain Abraham climbed with the knife and the wood, and came down with his son still alive. Later generations built the Temple on this same ridge — Scripture returns to a place centuries later, and this one it never leaves.
sites.name: THE LAND OF MORIAH
sites.place: The ridge that would become Zion
sites.quote: And Abraham called the name of that place Jehovahjireh: as it is said to this day, In the mount of the LORD it shall be seen.

sites.context: Abraham's altar and Jacob's ladder.
sites.description: A high point on the ridge route where Abraham pitched his tent, and where Jacob — running for his life — slept on a stone and saw a ladder set up to heaven. He called it the House of God.
sites.name: BETHEL
sites.place: The central watershed road
sites.quote: Surely the LORD is in this place; and I knew it not.

sites.context: Where Jacob becomes Israel.
sites.description: A lonely ford on the Jabbok where Jacob, returning home after twenty years, wrestled until daybreak and would not let go until he was blessed — and limped away with a new name.
sites.name: PENUEL
sites.place: The ford of the Jabbok
sites.quote: And Jacob called the name of the place Peniel: for I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved.

sites.context: Where a brother was sold, and a servant saw.
sites.description: A cistern town on the north road where Joseph's brothers sold him, and where, centuries later, Elisha's servant saw the mountain full of horses and chariots of fire. The pit and the opened eyes belong to the same ground.
sites.name: DOTHAN
sites.place: The pasture road toward the Jezreel
sites.quote: And they took him, and cast him into a pit: and the pit was empty, there was no water in it.

sites.archaeology: Magha'ir Shu'ayb · the oasis of Al-Bad'
sites.context: The bush, and the name I AM.
sites.description: The far country Moses fled to after he killed the Egyptian, where he kept Jethro's flock and turned aside to a bush that burned and was not consumed. The Exodus begins not in the brickyards, but with a shepherd taking off his shoes.
sites.name: MIDIAN
sites.place: The wilderness east of the Gulf of Aqaba
sites.quote: And he said, Draw not nigh hither: put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.

sites.context: Four hundred years of waiting, and one night of leaving.
sites.description: The fertile delta given to Joseph's family in the famine, and the brickyards their descendants were broken in. Excavation at Tell el-Dab'a shows a large Semitic population here long before it became the Ramesside capital.
sites.name: GOSHEN (RAMESES)
sites.place: Lower Egypt floodplain
sites.quote: And the children of Israel journeyed from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand on foot that were men, beside children.

sites.archaeology: The Bitter Lakes corridor · traditional sea crossing
sites.context: Dry land through the sea.
sites.description: The water that opened for a nation on foot and closed on the chariots that followed. Whether the crossing was the Bitter Lakes or a gulf further south, this is the night Israel stopped being slaves and started being a people.
sites.name: YAM SUPH (THE SEA)
sites.place: The reed sea between delta and wilderness
sites.quote: And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and the LORD caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all that night, and made the sea dry land, and the waters were divided.

sites.context: Water from the rock, and the first battle.
sites.description: A dry station in the wilderness where the people nearly stoned Moses for water, where the rock was struck, and where Amalek was held off only while Moses' hands stayed raised.
sites.name: REPHIDIM
sites.place: The last camp before the mountain
sites.quote: Behold, I will stand before thee there upon the rock in Horeb; and thou shalt smite the rock, and there shall come water out of it.

sites.context: The covenant, and the highest point on the road.
sites.description: The mountain of the Law, rising over 2,200 m out of the southern Sinai massif — the highest ground on the entire journey, by a wide margin. The Law was given here, and broken here, and given again.
sites.name: MOUNT SINAI (HOREB)
sites.place: Granite ranges above the Red Sea
sites.quote: And mount Sinai was altogether on a smoke, because the LORD descended upon it in fire.

sites.context: The turning point that cost a generation.
sites.description: The oasis that served as Israel's base for a generation. Twelve spies went out from here and ten came back afraid — and that refusal, at this spring, bought forty years of wandering.
sites.name: KADESH BARNEA
sites.place: The largest spring in northern Sinai
sites.quote: And they went and came to Moses… unto the wilderness of Paran, to Kadesh; and brought back word unto them.

sites.context: The last vantage point of Moses.
sites.description: The Moabite ridge looking out over the Jordan valley, nearly a kilometre above the river below. Moses climbed it, saw the whole land, and died within sight of the thing he had spent forty years walking toward.
sites.name: MOUNT NEBO
sites.place: The escarpment above the Dead Sea
sites.quote: I have caused thee to see it with thine eyes, but thou shalt not go over thither.

sites.archaeology: The Jordan ford camps east of Jericho
sites.context: Where Egypt's reproach was rolled away.
sites.description: The base camp after the crossing, where twelve stones from the riverbed stood as a sign, the manna ceased, and a new generation was marked for the land they had just entered.
sites.name: GILGAL
sites.place: The first camp west of Jordan
sites.quote: And the LORD said unto Joshua, This day have I rolled away the reproach of Egypt from off you. Wherefore the name of the place is called Gilgal unto this day.

sites.context: The gate into the promised land.
sites.description: A spring-fed oasis and one of the oldest continuously inhabited places known, sitting 258 m below sea level — the lowest ground on the journey, and the first city taken as Israel came into Canaan.
sites.name: JERICHO
sites.place: The lowest city on earth, −258 m
sites.quote: So the people shouted when the priests blew with the trumpets… and the wall fell down flat.

sites.archaeology: Ma'ayan Harod · the foot of Mount Gilboa
sites.context: Where a host was thinned to three hundred.
sites.description: The water where Gideon sent home the fearful and then the kneelers, until three hundred men who lapped like dogs were left to face a host like locusts. Pitchers, torches, and a shout — The sword of the LORD, and of Gideon.
sites.name: THE SPRING OF HAROD
sites.place: The spring under Gilboa
sites.quote: And the LORD said unto Gideon, By the three hundred men that lapped will I save you, and deliver the Midianites into thine hand.

sites.context: Where strength was a vow, and then a prayer.
sites.description: The ridge where a Nazirite was born, and the valley where he tore a lion, loved a Philistine, and at the last pulled a house down on himself. Strength and ruin share the same few miles of lowland.
sites.name: ZORAH & TIMNAH
sites.place: The Philistine border hills
sites.quote: And Samson called unto the LORD, and said, O Lord GOD, remember me, I pray thee, and strengthen me, I pray thee, only this once, O God.

sites.context: The last darkness before a king.
sites.description: The town that closes the book of Judges in horror, and later becomes Saul's capital. Between the outrage and the crown the refrain is the same: there was no king, and every man did what was right in his own eyes.
sites.name: GIBEAH OF BENJAMIN
sites.place: The hill just north of Jerusalem
sites.quote: In those days there was no king in Israel: every man did that which was right in his own eyes.

sites.context: Hitherto hath the LORD helped us.
sites.description: The assembly ground of the tribes, where Israel gathered against Benjamin, and where Samuel later set a stone and named it Ebenezer. The Judges end here; the kingdom is asked for on this ridge.
sites.name: MIZPAH
sites.place: The watchtower north of Gibeah
sites.quote: Then Samuel took a stone, and set it between Mizpeh and Shen, and called the name of it Ebenezer, saying, Hitherto hath the LORD helped us.

sites.context: The heart of the kingdom.
sites.description: Taken by David as the capital of a united kingdom and made the site of Solomon's Temple. Burned by Babylon in 586 BC, rebuilt after the exile, and argued over ever since.
sites.name: JERUSALEM (ZION)
sites.place: The ridge between the Kidron and the Hinnom
sites.quote: Nevertheless David took the strong hold of Zion: the same is the city of David.

sites.context: Where the tabernacle stood before Zion.
sites.description: The resting place of the tabernacle for generations, where Hannah prayed and Samuel heard his name in the night — and where the ark was lost to the Philistines when the priesthood failed.
sites.name: SHILOH
sites.place: The ridge road north of Bethel
sites.quote: And the whole congregation of the children of Israel assembled together at Shiloh, and set up the tabernacle of the congregation there.

sites.context: Where the Temple's cedar came from.
sites.description: The sea powers that supplied the cedar, the gold and the craftsmen for Solomon's Temple, and whose purple dye and alphabet travelled the whole Mediterranean. Ezekiel later sang its funeral.
sites.name: TYRE & SIDON
sites.place: A fortified island port
sites.quote: And Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants unto Solomon… for Hiram was ever a lover of David.

sites.context: The capital lost to Assyria.
sites.description: The capital Omri built on a defensible hill, famous for its ivory-inlaid palace and condemned for it by Amos and Hosea. Its fall in 722 BC ended the northern kingdom for good.
sites.name: SAMARIA (SEBASTE)
sites.place: An isolated hill above the Shechem road
sites.quote: In the ninth year of Hoshea the king of Assyria took Samaria, and carried Israel away into Assyria.

sites.context: The God that answereth by fire.
sites.description: The mountain where Elijah rebuilt an altar in twelve stones, soaked it three times, and called down fire in front of four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal. How long halt ye between two opinions, he asked, and the fire answered.
sites.name: MOUNT CARMEL
sites.place: The high ridge above the sea road
sites.quote: Then the fire of the LORD fell, and consumed the burnt sacrifice, and the wood, and the stones, and the dust, and licked up the water that was in the trench.

sites.archaeology: Tel Megiddo · the great gate & stables
sites.context: Where kings die at the pass.
sites.description: A fortress city on the narrow pass between the coast and the inland road — Solomonic gates, chariot cities, and the place good king Josiah fell. The valley below would later lend its name to Armageddon.
sites.name: MEGIDDO
sites.place: The pass that commands the plain
sites.quote: In his days Pharaoh-nechoh king of Egypt went up against the king of Assyria to the river Euphrates: and king Josiah went against him; and he slew him at Megiddo, when he had seen him.

sites.archaeology: Tel Lachish · the Assyrian siege ramp
sites.context: Where Assyria came up against Judah.
sites.description: The fortress Sennacherib took while Hezekiah watched from Jerusalem. The siege ramp still leans against the tell, and the palace reliefs in Nineveh show the same ramp from the other side — a city remembered by the army that broke it.
sites.name: LACHISH
sites.place: Judah's second city
sites.quote: Now in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah did Sennacherib king of Assyria come up against all the fenced cities of Judah, and took them.

sites.archaeology: The Barada oasis & the old city walls
sites.context: The northern rival, and the road north.
sites.description: The Aramaean capital watered by the Barada, fought over through the whole age of the kings. Naaman's rivers ran here, and he had to be talked into a muddier one.
sites.name: DAMASCUS
sites.place: The Barada river oasis
sites.quote: Are not Abana and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel?

sites.context: The power that carried off the north.
sites.description: The Assyrian capital on the Tigris, holding Ashurbanipal's library and some twelve kilometres of wall. Jonah preached here and it repented; Nahum promised the fall that came in 612 BC.
sites.name: NINEVEH
sites.place: The imperial Assyrian capital
sites.quote: Now Nineveh was an exceeding great city of three days' journey.

sites.context: Seventy years by the river.
sites.description: Nebuchadnezzar's capital of blue-glazed gates and processional ways, where Judah spent seventy years and where Daniel outlasted four kings. The exile ends where the journey began — back on the Euphrates.
sites.name: BABYLON
sites.place: The Euphrates metropolis
sites.quote: By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down, yea, we wept, when we remembered Zion.

sites.context: The court that signed the decree to return.
sites.description: The Achaemenid winter capital at the eastern end of the Royal Road, where Esther became queen for such a time as this, and where Nehemiah heard that the walls of Jerusalem were still down.
sites.name: SUSA (SHUSHAN)
sites.place: The royal Persian citadel
sites.quote: That in those days, when the king Ahasuerus sat on the throne of his kingdom, which was in Shushan the palace.

sites.context: The promise takes a body.
sites.description: The village Micah named seven hundred years early — little among the thousands of Judah, and the birthplace of David and of David's greater son. The journey turns here from promise to person.
sites.name: BETHLEHEM
sites.place: The shepherds' fields, six miles from Jerusalem
sites.quote: And she brought forth her firstborn son… and laid him in a manger; because there was no room for them in the inn.

sites.context: Thirty hidden years.
sites.description: A small Galilean village of no reputation — "can there any good thing come out of Nazareth?" — where thirty of the thirty-three years were quietly spent, and where the hometown crowd tried to throw him off a cliff.
sites.name: NAZARETH
sites.place: A hill village above the Jezreel valley
sites.quote: And he came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up: and, as his custom was, he went into the synagogue on the sabbath day, and stood up for to read.

sites.context: Where the ministry is opened from heaven.
sites.description: The same river Israel crossed into the land, and the water where John baptized — where the heavens opened, the Spirit descended, and a voice named the beloved Son before the public ministry began.
sites.name: THE JORDAN
sites.place: The river of the crossing and the baptism
sites.quote: And Jesus, when he was baptized, went up straightway out of the water: and, lo, the heavens were opened unto him.

sites.context: The ministry's home water.
sites.description: The lakeside town that became the base of operations — a customs post and fishing harbour where the first disciples were called off their boats, and where most of the miracles happened.
sites.name: CAPERNAUM & GALILEE
sites.place: The north shore, 210 m below sea level
sites.quote: Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.

sites.context: The hinge of the whole journey.
sites.description: A quarry face and a garden tomb just outside the city wall — five hundred metres from the Temple Mount, and the hinge the whole road has been bending toward since Ur.
sites.name: GOLGOTHA & THE TOMB
sites.place: The place of a skull
sites.quote: He is not here, but is risen.

sites.context: Where the Scriptures were opened.
sites.description: A road, an evening, and two people walking away from the city in disappointment — who had the whole of Moses and the prophets explained to them by a stranger, and only recognised him when he broke the bread.
sites.name: EMMAUS
sites.place: Threescore furlongs from Jerusalem
sites.quote: Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures?

sites.archaeology: The southern approach to the old city
sites.context: The persecutor is turned around.
sites.description: Not the city but the road outside it, where a man carrying warrants against the church was knocked flat by a light and stood up blind, and three days later became its most relentless missionary.
sites.name: THE DAMASCUS ROAD
sites.place: On the road, still short of the gate
sites.quote: And he fell to the earth, and heard a voice saying unto him, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?

sites.context: Where the mission was launched.
sites.description: Third city of the Roman empire, and the first church where Jew and Gentile ate at the same table. The base from which Paul and Barnabas were sent out — the hinge between the homeland and the world.
sites.name: ANTIOCH
sites.place: The Orontes valley gateway
sites.quote: And the disciples were called Christians first in Antioch.

sites.archaeology: Temple of Artemis · the great theatre
sites.context: Two years that shook Asia.
sites.description: A port and temple city where the gospel ran for two years, the silversmiths rioted over lost trade, and the magic books were burned in the street. Later the first of the seven churches to be written to.
sites.name: EPHESUS
sites.place: The harbour city of the Cayster
sites.quote: So mightily grew the word of God and prevailed.

sites.archaeology: The Bema · temple of Apollo · Acrocorinth
sites.context: The difficult church that got the best letters.
sites.description: A wealthy, rough port straddling the isthmus, where Paul stayed eighteen months and wrote to a church that argued about everything. The letters back to it are the most practical in the New Testament.
sites.name: CORINTH
sites.place: The isthmus between two seas
sites.quote: And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.

sites.archaeology: The Roman forum · prison tradition · river baptism site
sites.context: Where the gospel crosses into Europe.
sites.description: The first European landing of the gospel — a Roman colony where Lydia believed by the riverside, a jailer was baptized at midnight, and a letter later taught the church to rejoice always.
sites.name: PHILIPPI
sites.place: A colony on the Via Egnatia
sites.quote: And a vision appeared to Paul in the night; There stood a man of Macedonia, and prayed him, saying, Come over into Macedonia, and help us.

sites.context: The gospel reaches the capital.
sites.description: The capital Paul reached in chains and preached in for two years at his own hired house. Acts ends here mid-sentence, with the message loose in the empire and the prisoner still talking.
sites.name: ROME
sites.place: The centre of the known world
sites.quote: Preaching the kingdom of God… with all confidence, no man forbidding him.

sites.context: The last place, and the last word.
sites.description: A bare rock in the Aegean where an old man was sent to be forgotten, and where instead the last book was given — the road that started at a Chaldean city ends looking at a city coming down out of heaven.
sites.name: PATMOS
sites.place: A prison island off the coast of Asia
sites.quote: And I saw a new heaven and a new earth: for the first heaven and the first earth were passed away.

antioch.narrative: In the sprawling Syrian metropolis, Jews and Gentiles unite in the faith, commissioning Paul and Barnabas for their global mission.
antioch.quote: And the disciples were called Christians first in Antioch.
antioch.title: The Church at Antioch

babylon.narrative: Beneath the blue-glazed Ishtar Gate, Daniel and the exiles resolve in their hearts not to defile themselves with the king's meat.
babylon.quote: By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down, yea, we wept, when we remembered Zion.
babylon.title: Exile by the Euphrates

beersheba.narrative: At the edge of the southern desert, Abraham plants a tamarisk tree and calls on the name of the everlasting God.
beersheba.quote: Wherefore he called that place Beersheba; because there they sware both of them.
beersheba.title: The Well of Beersheba

bethel.narrative: Fleeing into the night with a stone for a pillow, Jacob beholds angels ascending and descending a stairway to heaven.
bethel.quote: Surely the LORD is in this place; and I knew it not.
bethel.title: Jacob's Ladder

bethlehem.narrative: Under the brilliance of the eastern star, shepherds find the newborn King of kings resting in a humble rock-cut manger.
bethlehem.quote: And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger.
bethlehem.title: The Birth of the Messiah

capernaum.narrative: On the shore of the sparkling Sea of Galilee, fishermen leave their nets, boats, and families to follow the Master.
capernaum.quote: Fear not; from henceforth thou shalt catch men.
capernaum.title: Fishers of Men

carmel.narrative: Before the prophets of Baal and all Israel, Elijah calls upon the God of Abraham, and fire consumes the soaked sacrifice.
carmel.quote: The God that answereth by fire, let him be God.
carmel.title: The Fire on Mount Carmel

corinth.narrative: A wealthy, rough port straddling the isthmus, where Paul stayed eighteen months and wrote to a church that argued about everything.
corinth.quote: And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.
corinth.title: Faith, Hope, Charity

damascus.narrative: The Syrian captain learns humility in the waters of Jordan, while Damascus remains the enduring crossroads of kings.
damascus.quote: Are not Abana and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel?
damascus.title: The Waters of Damascus

damascus-road.narrative: A blinding flash brighter than the midday sun strikes the persecutor to the earth, transforming Saul into the Apostle to the Gentiles.
damascus-road.quote: Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?
damascus-road.title: The Light from Heaven

dothan.narrative: Stripped of his coat of many colours, young Joseph is cast into an empty cistern before being sold into Egyptian bondage.
dothan.quote: Come now therefore, and let us slay him, and cast him into some pit.
dothan.title: The Pit of Dothan

emmaus.narrative: Walking at twilight, two sorrowful disciples have their eyes opened as the risen Lord breaks bread at their table.
emmaus.quote: Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures?
emmaus.title: The Road to Emmaus

ephesus.narrative: Standing against the silver shrines of Artemis, Paul ministers for three years as the Gospel sweeps through Asia Minor.
ephesus.quote: So mightily grew the word of God and prevailed.
ephesus.title: The Word Prevails at Ephesus

gibeah.narrative: From the rocky fortress of Gibeah, Jonathan and his armour-bearer scale the sharp crags of the pass to strike the Philistine garrison.
gibeah.quote: There is no restraint to the LORD to save by many or by few.
gibeah.title: The Pass of Bozez

gilgal.narrative: Twelve riverbed stones are hoisted from the riverbed and piled at Gilgal as a perpetual monument of divine deliverance.
gilgal.quote: What mean ye by these stones? Then ye shall let your children know, saying, Israel came over this Jordan on dry land.
gilgal.title: The Stones of Gilgal

golgotha.narrative: Outside the city gates, the Saviour yields up His spirit on the cross, and on the third day breaks the bonds of the tomb forever.
golgotha.quote: He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay.
golgotha.title: It is Finished

goshen.narrative: In the fertile delta under Egyptian taskmasters, Israel groans beneath heavy mortar until God remembers His covenant.
goshen.quote: And the children of Israel sighed by reason of the bondage, and they cried.
goshen.title: The Brickmakers of Goshen

haran.narrative: At the crossroads of the northern trade routes, the voice of the Almighty calls Abram southwest into the unknown.
haran.quote: Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father's house, unto a land that I will shew thee.
haran.title: The Call at Haran

harod.narrative: At the cool waters beneath Mount Gilboa, Gideon watches his warriors drink, paring the army down to three hundred clay jars and torches.
harod.quote: By the three hundred men that lapped will I save you, and deliver the Midianites into thine hand.
harod.title: The Spring of Harod

hebron.narrative: Beneath the ancient terebinth trees, Abraham pitches his tent and acquires the burial cave of Machpelah for his seed.
hebron.quote: Then Abram removed his tent, and came and dwelt in the plain of Mamre, which is in Hebron.
hebron.title: The Oaks of Mamre

jericho.narrative: After seven days of marching in solemn silence, the blast of rams' horns and the roar of the multitude bring down the fortress walls.
jericho.quote: So the people shouted when the priests blew with the trumpets... and the wall fell down flat.
jericho.title: The Trumpets of Jericho

jerusalem.narrative: Scaling the water shaft of the Jebusite stronghold, David establishes the royal citadel and brings up the Ark with joy.
jerusalem.quote: So David dwelt in the fort, and called it the city of David.
jerusalem.title: Zion, the City of David

jordan.narrative: As Jesus rises from the rushing waters of the Jordan, the Holy Spirit descends like a dove and the Father's voice speaks.
jordan.quote: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.
jordan.title: The Heavens Opened

kadesh.narrative: Returning from Canaan bearing giant clusters of grapes, Caleb and Joshua urge the congregation to trust the LORD.
kadesh.quote: The land, which we passed through to search it, is an exceeding good land.
kadesh.title: The Spies of Kadesh

lachish.narrative: Hezekiah's fortress burns under Assyrian catapults, but Jerusalem looks to Isaiah's God for shelter.
lachish.quote: Be strong and courageous, be not afraid nor dismayed for the king of Assyria: for there be more with us than with him.
lachish.title: The Siege of Lachish

megiddo.narrative: The ancient strategic pass and fortress where kings clashed and where prophecies foreshadow the final battle.
megiddo.quote: And king Josiah went against him; and he slew him at Megiddo.
megiddo.title: The Plain of Megiddo

midian.narrative: Tending sheep on the backside of the desert, Moses stops before a desert thorn bush blazing with fire yet unconsumed.
midian.quote: Put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.
midian.title: The Burning Bush

mizpah.narrative: Samuel raises a standing stone on the ridge, naming it Ebenezer in thanksgiving for the thunderous deliverance of Israel.
mizpah.quote: Hitherto hath the LORD helped us.
mizpah.title: The Stone of Help

moriah.narrative: Ascending the silent ridge with wood and fire, Abraham's faith is proved as a ram caught in the thicket is offered instead.
moriah.quote: God will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering, my son.
moriah.title: The Mount of Moriah

nazareth.narrative: Standing in the hilltop synagogue of his childhood, Jesus unrolls the scroll of Isaiah and proclaims liberty to the captives.
nazareth.quote: This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears.
nazareth.title: The Spirit of the Lord

nebo.narrative: Standing on the windswept summit of Pisgah, the aged prophet gazes across the Jordan Valley at the inheritance of Israel.
nebo.quote: I have caused thee to see it with thine eyes, but thou shalt not go over thither.
nebo.title: The Vista from Mount Nebo

nineveh.narrative: Walking three days through the colossal Assyrian capital, Jonah's single message brings the king and citizens to sackcloth and ashes.
nineveh.quote: Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown. So the people of Nineveh believed God.
nineveh.title: The Preacher at Nineveh

patmos.narrative: Exiled on the rocky Aegean island on the Lord's Day, John beholds the glorified Christ and the celestial New Jerusalem coming down from heaven.
patmos.quote: I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending, saith the Lord, which is, and which was, and which is to come, the Almighty.
patmos.title: The Revelation on Patmos

penuel.narrative: At the solitary ford of the Jabbok, Jacob wrestles through the night and limps into the sunrise bearing the name Israel.
penuel.quote: I will not let thee go, except thou bless me.
penuel.title: The Wrestling at Penuel

philippi.narrative: Beaten and bound in the inner dungeon, midnight hymns bring an earthquake that shakes the foundations and frees the captives.
philippi.quote: And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them.
philippi.title: Songs at Midnight in Philippi

rephidim.narrative: In the parched wilderness, Moses strikes the granite crag, and living water gushes forth to quench the thirst of the multitude.
rephidim.quote: Behold, I will stand before thee there upon the rock in Horeb; and thou shalt smite the rock.
rephidim.title: Water from the Rock

rome.narrative: Chained to a Roman soldier in his hired house, Paul writes the epistles that would anchor churches across the ages.
rome.quote: Preaching the kingdom of God, and teaching those things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ, with all confidence.
rome.title: The Prisoner in Rome

samaria.narrative: The hilltop capital of Israel falls to the Assyrian siege engines as the prophets' warnings come to pass.
samaria.quote: The houses of ivory shall perish, and the great houses shall have an end, saith the LORD.
samaria.title: The Ivory Houses of Samaria

shechem.narrative: Standing between the heights of Ebal and Gerizim, Abram builds an altar of stone to mark the land of promise.
shechem.quote: Unto thy seed will I give this land: and there builded he an altar unto the LORD.
shechem.title: The First Altar in Canaan

shiloh.narrative: In the sanctuary where the lamp of God burns through the night, a young boy hears his name called in the darkness.
shiloh.quote: Speak, LORD; for thy servant heareth.
shiloh.title: The Voice at Shiloh

sinai.narrative: Wrapped in thunder, lightning, and thick cloud, Moses ascends into the presence of God to receive the stone tablets.
sinai.quote: And mount Sinai was altogether on a smoke, because the LORD descended upon it in fire.
sinai.title: The Glory on Mount Sinai

susa.narrative: In the marble halls of the Persian winter palace, Queen Esther approaches King Ahasuerus unbidden to plead for her people.
susa.title: For Such a Time as This

tyre.narrative: Gigantic cedar beams are floated down the Mediterranean coast to build the glorious house of the LORD on Mount Moriah.
tyre.quote: Now therefore command thou that they hew me cedar trees out of Lebanon.
tyre.title: The Cedars of Lebanon

ur.narrative: Leaving the shadow of the great ziggurat behind, Abram sets out with his household into the desert on the strength of an unseen promise.
ur.quote: And they went forth with them from Ur of the Chaldees, to go into the land of Canaan.
ur.title: Abram Departs Ur

yam-suph.narrative: With Pharaoh's chariots pursuing behind and waters before, Moses lifts his rod as the sea splits into towering walls of water.
yam-suph.quote: Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the LORD.
yam-suph.title: The Parting of the Sea

zorah.narrative: Amid the rocky crags of the Sorek Valley, the Nazarite champion breaks his bonds and scatters the Philistine host.
zorah.quote: And the Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon him... and he found a new jawbone of an ass.
zorah.title: The Strong Man of Dan
